tagline: Leading marketplace for asset disposition and auction services globally
hero_kpi_rationale: GTV is a key metric measuring the total value of transactions conducted on the company's asset disposition platforms and marketplaces, reflecting operational efficiency and growth in transaction volume.

kpis.name: Gross Transaction Value
kpis.explanation: Gross Transaction Value — total value transacted on the platform.
kpis.description: GTV represents the total value of all items sold through the company's online auctions and marketplaces.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue includes service revenues and revenues from sales of inventory

kpis.name: Service Revenue
kpis.description: Service revenue represents a major component of the company's total revenue.

kpis.name: Inventory Sales Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the Inventory Sales segment.
kpis.description: Inventory sales revenue represents significant year-over-year growth.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Net Income — bottom-line profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income increases by 4% to $427.6 million

kpis.name: Adjusted Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization
kpis.explanation: Adjusted EBITDA — EBITDA excluding non-recurring or one-off items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA increases by 7% to $1.4 billion

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.explanation: Operating Income — profit from core business operations.
kpis.description: Operating income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL for the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).

kpis.name: Diluted EPS
kpis.explanation: Diluted Earnings Per Share — EPS including all convertible securities.
kpis.description: Diluted EPS extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL for the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Dividend Per Share — total dividends paid divided by shares outstanding.
kpis.description: Dividend per share paid annually, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend cut risk, monitor payout sustainability

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.explanation: Capital Return — total cash returned to shareholders (dividends + buybacks).
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Payout Ratio — dividends paid divided by net income.
kpis.description: Payout ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Shareholder returns growing, dividend policy supportive

stories_kpis.name: Gross Transaction Value in 2025
stories_kpis.explanation: Total value of transactions carried out on the company's auctions and online marketplaces in 2025.
stories_kpis.description: GTV in 2025 reached $16.2 billion, reflecting 2% year-over-year growth.

stories_kpis.name: Total Revenue Growth in 2025
stories_kpis.explanation: Increase in total enterprise revenue in 2025.
stories_kpis.description: Total revenue increased 7% to $4.6 billion in 2025, with strong contribution from inventory sales, which rose 18%.
stories_kpis.signal: Significant growth in total revenue driven by inventory sales

ai_positioning.summary: The company RBA does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and IT systems risks
risks.summary: RBA continuously monitors cybersecurity threats through a dedicated committee and an experienced security officer. A breach could disrupt auction operations and compromise customer data.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned first in the available excerpt, with a detailed governance framework (Audit Committee, CISO, quarterly SSC), signaling active concern. The language remains descriptive rather than alarmist, but cybersecurity category weighting is high by regulatory convention.

risks.title: Dependence on key interim executives (COO/CTO)
risks.summary: The Chief Operating Officer is temporarily assuming the role of Chief Technology Officer. If this individual were to leave the company, two critical functions would simultaneously be vacant.
risks.score_rationale: The excerpt indicates that the COO is serving as interim CTO, signaling a strategic-level vacancy. While the language is factual, this situation creates a concentration of responsibilities on a single individual, a new trend compared to a stable organizational structure.

risks.title: Tax risk related to foreign shareholders (Canada)
risks.summary: U.S. shareholders of RBA may be subject to Canadian withholding taxes on dividends. Changes in Canadian tax law could increase this burden without notice.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned at the end of the document in the tax section, with cautious language ('no assurance can be given'). Risk is stable and governed by the Canada-U.S. tax treaty, but potential legislative changes could affect non-resident investors.

risks.title: Risk of foreign control under the Canadian Investment Act
risks.summary: Any takeover of RBA by a non-Canadian investor must be approved by the Canadian government. This may hinder certain merger and acquisition activities or discourage takeover bids.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned mid-document, with neutral but precise language regarding the requirement for ministerial approval. Risk is stable and limited to control acquisitions, but it represents a real regulatory constraint for RBA as a Canadian publicly traded company.

risks.title: Liquidity risk related to holding company status with no direct assets
risks.summary: RBA is a holding company with no assets of its own. If its subsidiaries do not generate sufficient revenues, it will be unable to pay dividends or meet its financial obligations.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in the dividends section, with direct language ('no material assets other than the shares of its subsidiaries'). This structural risk is stable but significant: the ability to pay dividends depends entirely on subsidiaries, creating vulnerability in case of operational difficulties.

risks.title: Geographic concentration of real estate assets in the United States
risks.summary: Three-quarters of RBA's operating sites are located in the United States. An economic crisis or major natural disaster in this country could significantly disrupt all operations.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned mid-document in the properties section, with descriptive language. Of 333 sites, 250 are in the United States, representing a notable geographic concentration. Risk is stable, but a natural disaster or U.S. economic crisis would have a disproportionate impact.

governance.voting_structure_note: One share, one vote (standard structure, ordinary shares).
